query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for structural use under extreme-temperature conditions, what single intervention could improve high-temperature oxygen resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the temperature, atmosphere, and exposure conditions under which it should work, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Pack aluminization of refractory high-entropy alloys will improve their high‐temperature oxygen resistance by forming a continuous, adherent alumina scale that retards oxygen ingress.
generation.material_initial_state: A refractory high-entropy alloy produced with its standard processing route, having its baseline composition without any surface modifications.
generation.intervention: A pack aluminization surface treatment that diffuses aluminum into the alloy surface to promote in situ formation of an alumina (Al2O3) layer.
generation.conditions: Exposing treated and untreated samples at 1000°C in air (approximately 21% O2) for 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, adherent alumina scale at the alloy surface.
generation.mechanism: The aluminization treatment elevates the surface aluminum concentration so that, upon high-temperature exposure, a thermodynamically stable alumina scale forms. This oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier, significantly slowing further oxygen ingress and subsequent oxidation of the underlying alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: The aluminized alloy will show a markedly reduced oxidation weight gain and thinner oxide layer compared to the untreated alloy under the same testing conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys exposed at 1000°C in air for 100 hours typically develop a thicker, less protective oxide scale with higher weight gain.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected only if sufficient aluminum is available at the surface to form a continuous scale, and it may not apply to alloy compositions or aluminization treatments that do not provide the necessary diffusion kinetics or scale adhesion.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the oxidation improvement will depend on specific processing parameters and alloy composition; further quantitative study is required to exactly determine the performance enhancement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples from the same refractory high-entropy alloy. Subject one set to a pack aluminization treatment and leave the other untreated. Expose both sets to 1000°C in air (21% O2) for 100 hours. Afterwards, analyze oxidation weight gain using thermogravimetric analysis and examine the oxide layer thickness and morphology using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction.
measurements: Oxidation weight gain per unit area
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pack aluminized samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation weight gain and oxide scale thickness, or if the oxide scale does not predominantly consist of a continuous alumina layer compared to the untreated samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
